questions: Do the iteration 5 metrics differ from iteration 0 (score 26.0449) and iteration 4 (score 25.7177)? If they match exactly, please confirm the seed and track used.
Does moving the sensors to y = 0.07 m reduce max_error below 0.06 m, or reduce line_loss_events below one on the s-bend and slalom?
Does steering_oscillation rise with the forward lead? If so, the lead is causing overshoot and should be reduced again.
Please report per-step telemetry for one trial per track, showing the step and progress where the first line loss begins, and whether it starts at the course start or at a specific bend.

intent: Revert wheel_radius to 0.03 m (the iteration 4 change scored lower) and move the sensor row forward to y = 0.07 m, with the 16 mm footprint and ±0.03 m spread kept. Test whether earlier sensing of the tape gives enough lead to stop the single early line loss on the s-bend and slalom. Expect max_error to fall below 0.06 m and line_loss_events to drop toward zero. If the metrics match iteration 0 or 4 exactly, the lead has no effect and the controller gain is the next lever.
learning: Iterations 0 to 4 show that sensor spread (0.02 to 0.03 m), footprint (12 to 16 mm), wheel track (0.10 to 0.12 m) and wheel radius (0.03 to 0.04 m) do not lift max_error above the 0.06 m floor or remove the single line loss. Iteration 4 moved metrics slightly, so the pipeline is live. The remaining untested sensor lever is the forward lead. If the lead does not change the outcome, geometry is exhausted for the current controller, and the Integrator should move to controller gain (kp 2.0 to 3.0) on this geometry.
rationale:
Iteration 4 changed only wheel_radius (0.03 to 0.04 m). Metrics moved, so the pipeline is live. Score fell from 26.0449 (iteration 0 baseline, radius 0.03 m, track 0.12 m) to 25.7177. On the oval, progress fell from 0.115 to 0.1125 and max_error stayed at 0.060 to 0.061 m. Every trial still ended off track after one line-loss event. Across five geometry families (spread, footprint, wheel track, wheel radius), max_error has stayed at 0.060 to 0.061 m and line loss has stayed at one per trial. That points to the early steering response, not sensor visibility or track width, as the limit. The Integrator's rule (b) also says that when line loss persists at max_error near 0.06 m, the next lever is controller gain, not geometry.

The geometry decisions are: (1) revert wheel_radius to 0.03 m, since the 0.04 m test scored lower; (2) keep wheel_track 0.12 m, sensor_size 0.016 m and the ±0.03 m spread, which together gave the best-supported platform; (3) move the sensor row forward from y = 0.05 m to y = 0.07 m. This is the one remaining sensor-geometry lever that gives the controller more lead time before the robot reaches the edge of the tape. It is a single-variable change from iteration 4 once radius is reverted, so any metric change can be attributed to the lead. I expect a small reduction in max_error on the s-bend and slalom if the lead helps. If the metrics match iteration 4 or 0 exactly, the lead has no effect and the controller gain is the limit.
